---
title: "Optimised Glider II"
---

A chronological record of questions asked about a 300 mm span foam glider optimised for minimum sink rate in trimmed glide. Each **chapter**
is one model — a vehicle, a fidelity, a method — and each **entry** is one
question asked of it, answered by code that runs when the page renders.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Specified

True of every chapter, and inherited by any new one:

1. **Span**: 300 mm, fixed tip to tip.
2. **Construction**: flat foam sheet, cut and assembled by hand.
3. **Objective**: minimum sink rate in trimmed glide.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Assumed

1. **Still air**, no thermals and no wind gradient.
2. **Rigid airframe**, no aeroelastic deflection under load.
:::

## How the chapters relate

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
# GENERATED FROM THE CHAPTERS, never drawn by hand (rule 34 keeps this block).
#
# Reads source, executes none of it: no chapter model is imported or solved, so
# this page stays free to render and has no cross-chapter value dependency.
# `create_chapter` deletes this page's freeze when it scaffolds a chapter,
# because rule 12 cannot -- the root index belongs to no chapter, so nothing
# else would notice a seventh node was missing.
#
# `flowchart`, not `graph`: the same diagram, laid out by the current engine
# rather than the legacy one, which routes edges and packs nodes better and is
# what mermaid's own docs use now.
#
# TOP DOWN. Sideways was tried and the lineage is currently a straight line --
# six chapters, no branching -- so LR drew a 1900px strip that shrank the text
# to nothing and scrolled the page sideways, which `styles.css` exists to
# prevent everywhere else. A line reads fine down a page, which already
# scrolls that way. When a chapter finally branches, LR is worth revisiting.
#
# THE ARROWS CARRY THE TEXT AND THE NODES DO NOT. A chapter's title and the
# change that produced it are the same fact -- "Fuselage model" reached by
# "fuselage, 200 mm" -- so only one of them should be on the page. Putting it
# on the ARROW makes the picture read as a sequence of changes rather than a
# list of names, which is what a lineage is: the node is the design at that
# point, and the label before it says what made it that.
#
# The nodes stay clickable with no text in them. `click` binds to the node id,
# not its label, so an empty node is still the link to its chapter -- and the
# hover title carries the name for anyone who wants it.
#
# `summary:` is written in the "what it became" form, not "from → to": the
# arrow already carries the from, by pointing out of it.
import pathlib
import re

_TITLE = re.compile(r'^title:\s*"(.+)"\s*$', re.M)


def _fork(_d):
    """`_fork.yml`'s parent and summary. Flat by design -- see lint.read_fork."""
    _f = _d / "_fork.yml"
    if not _f.exists():
        return None, ""
    _t = _f.read_text()
    _p = re.search(r"^parent:\s*(.+?)\s*$", _t, re.M)
    _s = re.search(r'^summary:\s*"?(.+?)"?\s*$', _t, re.M)
    return (_p.group(1).strip() if _p else None), (_s.group(1).strip() if _s else "")


_chapters = sorted(p for p in pathlib.Path("chapters").iterdir() if p.is_dir())
_titles, _parent, _label = {}, {}, {}
for _c in _chapters:
    _index = _c / "index.qmd"
    _m = _TITLE.search(_index.read_text()) if _index.exists() else None
    _titles[_c.name] = _m.group(1) if _m else _c.name
    # Only a parent that still exists: a fork naming a renamed chapter should
    # leave a root node rather than a dangling edge.
    _p, _s = _fork(_c)
    if _p and (pathlib.Path("chapters") / _p).is_dir():
        _parent[_c.name] = _p
        # Mermaid reads a quoted edge label as a MARKDOWN string, so a summary
        # beginning "+ " or "- " renders as the literal "Unsupported markdown:
        # list" in place of the label. Seen on the page, not in any check.
        _label[_c.name] = re.sub(r"^\s*[-+*]\s+", "", _s)

_id = lambda s: "c" + re.sub(r"[^0-9A-Za-z]", "", s)
# A leaf is a chapter nothing was forked from: where a line of work reached,
# and the reason the "Where to start" paragraph could go -- the picture says it.
_leaves = {c.name for c in _chapters} - set(_parent.values())
print("```{mermaid}")
print("flowchart TD")
print("  classDef node fill:#fff,stroke:#9aa0a6,stroke-width:2px")
print("  classDef head fill:#e8f0fe,stroke:#4285f4,stroke-width:3px")
for _c in _chapters:
    print(f'  {_id(_c.name)}(( ))')
    print(f'  click {_id(_c.name)} "chapters/{_c.name}/index.html" '
          f'"{_titles[_c.name]}"')
    print(f"  class {_id(_c.name)} {'head' if _c.name in _leaves else 'node'}")
for _c in _chapters:
    if _c.name not in _parent:
        continue
    _e = f'-->|"{_label[_c.name]}"|' if _label[_c.name] else "-->"
    print(f"  {_id(_parent[_c.name])} {_e} {_id(_c.name)}")
print("```")
```
